pass_a_gloss: You heard. Paul in First Corinthians lists gifts including prophecy, saying one Spirit works all, giving each as He chooses—truly, not as slaves. The Spirit is Christ’s person, giving us prophecy’s Spirit; prophecy’s Spirit is the prophets’ person, the gift is the Spirit, Law is shadow—Law shadows future good. Prophets lived in us and in Law’s shadow. Prophetic gift aims at all prophecy’s end: Christ, from Christ—Christ ends Law and prophets. Could say from apostles and believers: in Him we live, move, are—we would live in His shadow.
pass_b_english: You were told. Moreover, in the First Epistle to the Corinthians, when Paul speaks of the spiritual gifts—among which is prophecy—he says: "All these things are energized by one and the same Spirit, who distributes to each individually as He wills." This means authoritatively, not servilely. One might say that the Spirit is the person of Christ, the One who bestowed upon us the Spirit of prophecy; for this very Spirit of prophecy is the person of the prophets, while the Spirit itself is the gift, and the Law is but a shadow—since "the Law has a shadow of the good things to come." Thus, the prophets lived within us and within the shadow of the Law. Therefore, the prophetic gift, toward which every manifestation of prophecy looks as its goal, is Christ, that is, from Christ. For "Christ is the end of the Law and the prophets." Moreover, it could be said even from the person of the apostles and the believers: "For in Him we live and move and have our being"—of whom we said that we would live in His shadow.
